Learned: also paths.py default vault was 'DRA BRAINS' (space) not 'dra-brains' -> cold tier would silently fail on a fresh Windows clone. content:
Voice speech quality fixes (2026-08-05):

1) Mojibake: harness.run() used subprocess text=True which defaults to cp1252 on Windows, turning UTF-8 LLM output into garbled characters like "â€"". Fixed by adding encoding="utf-8", errors="replace". Also strips ANSI escape codes (\(\x1b[...\) sequences) from opencode output.

2) Markdown spoken aloud: edge-tts was reading **bold**, _italic_, backticks, # headers, - bullets, [links], > quotes aloud as literal punctuation. New text_for_speech() in tts_streaming.py strips all markdown syntax before TTS).

3. Continuous speech: synthesis was per-sentence serially. New _speak_pipelined() in mode.py uses a producer-consumer pattern: synthesizer daemon thread writes WAVs to a bounded queue while the main thread plays them back, overlapping the edge-tts network round trip for sentence N+1 with the playback of sentence N. No more dead air between sentences.

Also made audio.play_ffmpeg() blocking (subprocess.run instead of Popen) because the pipeline requires ordered playback.
title: Voice quality: mojibake + markdown + pauses fixed

content:
Voice mode conversational quality (2026-08-05): Allan complained replies read like briefing reports. Root cause: each voice turn spawned a fresh `opencode run` with a bare transcript — no conversation context, no voice instruction. Fix in miloctl/voice/mode.py:
1. _build_voice_prompt(): question FIRST, style note appended LAST in a parenthetical ("Answer briefly and naturally, like spoken conversation. No bullet points, no headings, no bold text, no numbered lists."). Instructions at the FRONT get acknowledged instead of obeyed ("Got it, I'm here, what's on your mind?") — that was the tested failure mode.
2. Conversation history: last 6 turns (12 entries) ride along in the prompt so the fresh agent keeps context. Verified turn 2 references projects from turn 1.
3. MAX_SPEECH_SENTENCES=3: only the first 3 sentences are synthesized/speken. Free models (deepseek-v4-flash-free via opencode) ignore brevity instructions — a hard cap beats a hint. Full reply still shows in terminal.
Behavior notes: opencode run answers can be empty or inconsistent on this free model; can't rely on it for fast iteration. Tool-use (milo_mem_context, sessions_search) makes replies slow — the prompt tries to discourage it but the model often ignores.
commit 22b9dd7, 99 tests.

content: Windows Task Scheduler + milo routines: two silent failures found & fixed (commit be91ad3). (1) schtasks CLI defaults DisallowStartIfOnBatteries=true and StopIfGoingOnBatteries=true — on a laptop on battery the MiloRoutines task NEVER fires, silently, since registration. The CLI has no flag to disable this; fix is to register via task XML (`schtasks /Create /XML`) with `<DisallowStartIfOnBatteries>false</DisallowStartIfOnBatteries>`, `<StopIfGoingOnBatteries>false</StopIfGoingOnBatteries>`, `<StartWhenAvailable>true</StartWhenAvailable>`. (2) `--quiet` is a TOP-LEVEL argparse flag in milo, so `routines tick --quiet` exits 2; must be `--quiet routines tick`. (3) `scheduler.healthy()` now distinguishes registered from firing (checks Last Result 267011 / Last Run Time 11/30/1999 = never executed) and `milo doctor` reports it. Verification method: schtasks /query /tn MiloRoutines /fo LIST /v — Last Result 0 = healthy; check cron.json last_status/runs; vault git log shows "Milo: vault sync" pushes.
title: MiloRoutines task: battery block + --quiet order fix
